Engineering Leadership Development Program - Software Engineer (Various Locations) Job Details | L3HHCM20
Melbourne, FL
Full-time

New Grad

L3Harris Technologies offers a three-year rotational Engineering Leadership Development Program designed to accelerate the development of qualified engineers through exposure to different programs, business units, locations, and stages of the design life cycle. The Software Engineer will develop and test embedded software, collaborate across engineering functions, and participate in software development activities for advanced tactical radio equipment.
Aerospace

Responsibilities
Apply computer science, engineering, and mathematical analysis concepts and principles in the development of software for the target application
Work closely with cross functional members of the engineering organization to develop and evaluate interfaces between hardware and software, and operational performance requirements and design of the overall system
Support and participate in all phases of the software development life cycle, including requirements analysis, design, implementation, integration, and test of embedded software for real-time control of advanced tactical radio equipment
Develop software test procedures, software programs, and related documentation
Utilize modeling tools and equipment to establish operating data, conduct experimental tests, and evaluate results
Participate in peer reviews, identify, track and repair defects
Utilize a variety of software languages (i.e., C++, C#, C, Java, Ruby, HTML5, XML, SQL, Perl, Python, Ajax, Qt) on Windows, Linux, mobile platforms, and embedded real time operating systems (VxWorks, Linux, QNX, Integrity, Windows CE, and others for Motorola, Intel, TI, and custom processor designs)

Required
To be eligible, applicants must be pursuing a Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Engineering Mechanics, Materials Science Engineering or have completed their Bachelor's degree within the last 12 months, regardless of age
Ability to relocate every 12 months for the 3-year duration of the program
Preferred
CAD or analysis (FEA) tools exposure, and/or experience in mechanical design or analysis of electronic systems, structures and mechanisms
Familiarity with transducer instrumentation, data collection and or automation and software programming for numerical analysis
Must be able to generate free body diagrams, determine reaction forces, calculate internal loads, and develop shear and moment diagrams
Working knowledge of one programming language
Benefits
Participants are also paired with a mentor to guide their development through the program.
